Compiled characters.v1.json matches editorial.json for every body, gate and subtitle in both editions, and every thread epithet matches its card subtitle. The fixes introduced one major regression (the Charles McCarthy [4:37] snapshot) and three minor gating or accuracy slips. Applying the four exact fixes below should make the package acceptable.

newIssues.problem: The new [4:37] snapshot (added for S4-06) replaces the [4:17] snapshot. It reverts to the present tense ('rents Hatherley Farm') and drops the fact that he went to Boscombe Pool and never came back alive. From [4:37] until [4:208], tapping the murder victim's name shows a card that reads as if he were alive and says nothing about his death, which is the central fact of the story.
newIssues.fix: [4:37] snapshot body: "A former Australian colonist who rented Hatherley Farm from his old acquaintance John Turner, a widower with one son, James. On Monday 3 June he walked to Boscombe Pool for an important three o’clock appointment and never came back alive. His son describes him as cold and forbidding in manner and not a popular man."

newIssues.problem: The [7:190] snapshot now ends 'Ryder calls her Maggie.', but the name Maggie first appears at [7:194] (and [7:201]). This is a four-paragraph early reveal of a first name. It gives away no plot, but it is inconsistent with the gating standard.
newIssues.fix: Remove " Ryder calls her Maggie." from the [7:190] body. Add a snapshot after [7,194] with body: "James Ryder’s sister, married to a man named Oakshott. She fattens geese for the market in Brixton Road and had promised her brother a goose for Christmas. Ryder calls her Maggie."

newIssues.problem: The new [9:137] snapshot says he 'plots a ten-mile circle'. At [9:137] the text says only 'drawing a circle with Eyford for its centre'; the ten-mile radius is given at [9:138]. This is trivial.
newIssues.fix: [9:137] body: "A police inspector, here of Scotland Yard (an inspector Bradstreet also appears at Bow Street in the Hugh Boone affair). He travels to Eyford with Holmes, Watson and Hatherley and draws a circle on the county map with Eyford at its centre to find the house."

newIssues.problem: The [11:133] snapshot says she 'served the coffee while Holder spoke of the coronet'. At [11:42] Holder says Lucy 'had brought in the coffee' and he is 'sure, left the room', though he cannot swear the door was closed. The card contradicts his account.
newIssues.fix: [11:133] body: "The Holders’ second waiting-maid, in service only a few months. She brought in the coffee on the evening Holder spoke of the coronet; he believes she had left the room, but Mary suggests she may have overheard him. That night Mary saw her slipping back in at the kitchen door after meeting her sweetheart, the greengrocer Francis Prosper."
